---
title: "Update software"
---

Use this page for routine maintenance after a workstation has already been installed. The workflow updates this repository, reapplies the Ansible-managed lab stack, and checks for manually installed Fedora packages that are not documented in the setup.

## Routine workflow

Run these commands from the `workstation-setup` repository:

```sh
git pull
make lab-stack
make audit-packages
```

The explicit Ansible equivalents are:

```sh
git pull
ansible-playbook -i inventory -K playbooks/lab-stack.yml
ansible-playbook -i inventory -K playbooks/audit-unmanaged-packages.yml
```

Use `dnf list installed` or `dnf repoquery --userinstalled` when investigating local package state. AI coding tools can help draft Ansible changes, but review package names and repository changes before committing them.

::: {.callout-note title="What is an unmanaged package?"}

An unmanaged package is a package that is:

- manually installed on the workstation,
- not declared in this repository's Ansible-managed package list,
- and not allowlisted by exact name or allowlist pattern.

:::

## How filtering works

Fedora Workstation can report many base/system packages as user-installed. To keep this audit actionable, this repository uses:

- exact allowlist entries (`package_audit_allowlist`), and
- regex allowlist patterns (`package_audit_allowlist_patterns`).

These filters intentionally suppress expected Fedora Workstation/base noise. Packages that reflect deliberate workstation choices should be added to Ansible-managed package lists.

## Resolve audit findings

Choose one resolution for each finding:

- Add the package to an Ansible-managed package list when all lab workstations should install and maintain it.
- Add the package to `package_audit_allowlist` when it is an intentional local exception by exact package name.
- Add a targeted regex to `package_audit_allowlist_patterns` only for expected Fedora/system package families where exact names are too noisy.

Keep allowlist patterns narrow. Broad patterns can hide real workstation drift.
